Lite-On Technology UBS Research
Executive Summary
We initiate coverage of Lite-On Technology with a Buy rating and NT$400 price target, 
based on 20x our 2028E EPS of NT$20.0, or approximately 25x our 2027E EPS of NT
$16.0. The stock has already re-rated materially as investors recognize its improving 
participation in AI power, but we believe the change in the earnings base is structural. 
Lite-On has spent several years exiting lower-return businesses, improving its margin 
structure and redirecting investment toward Cloud & AIoT, where AI server power is now 
becoming a meaningful growth and earnings driver. Our target multiple remains below 
the roughly 22x level at which the broader power-supply peer group trades, reflecting 
Lite-On’s later entry and still-developing customer breadth. We forecast revenue growth 
of 31%/38%/25% in 2026/27/28 and EPS growth of 63%/47%/25%, supported by a 
rising cloud mix and operating leverage.
Lite-On is moving from proving participation to scaling in AI power
The core change in our thesis is that Lite-On no longer needs to prove that it can enter AI 
server power; it increasingly needs to demonstrate how far it can scale. AI server PSU 
shipments began ramping in late 2024/2025, customer qualifications have broadened, 
and the company is moving beyond individual power modules into larger power shelves, 
BBU/energy-management systems and eventually dedicated high-voltage power racks. 
Importantly, our checks suggest the power-rack opportunity is already becoming 
tangible on custom ASICs: we expect Lite-On to begin ramping a dedicated 48V power 
rack for its top ASIC client from late 2026, before stepping up to an ~800V/MW-class 
architecture with the following generation from late 2027. Lite-On remains well behind 
Delta in absolute AI power scale and breadth, but our forecasts do not require it to close 
that gap. The base case assumes only modest GPU-server share and stronger positions in 
selected custom-ASIC programs, leaving additional CSP wins as potential upside rather 
than a prerequisite.
AI power growth is a watts story, not an 800V adoption call
Our companion AI Power report (link) estimates industry AI server power-electronics 
TAM rising from approximately US$6.6bn in 2025 to US$91.1bn in 2030, a 69% CAGR. 
AI server rack shipments grow only around 12% CAGR in our model; the much larger 
drivers are a roughly 39% CAGR in average rack power and 55% CAGR in annual IT GW 
deployed, supplemented by higher power-system content per watt. This distinction 
matters for Lite-On. We expect strong 2026–27 AI power growth even if NVIDIA’s initial 
transition to dedicated 800V power racks is slower than previously expected. Higher 
accelerator shipments, the transition at its top ASIC customer to a richer 48V followed 
by 800V power rack, AMD’s move toward rack-scale systems and increasing custom-
ASIC rack density should drive substantial growth before widespread native 800V 
adoption, which should start with its ASIC customer from late 2027. The 400/800V 
transition becomes a more meaningful incremental content opportunity from 2028 
onward rather than the foundation of our near-term estimates.
ASIC exposure is a differentiator, while concentration is a risk
Lite-On is largely exposed to custom-ASIC power relative to the industry. We estimate 
ASIC programs contribute roughly two-thirds of its modeled AI power exposure over 
much of our forecast period, compared with custom ASICs representing roughly 40–
50% of industry AI power TAM. This creates both opportunity and concentration risk. 
ASIC systems are moving toward more accelerators per rack, higher BBU attachment 
and increasingly rack-level power architectures, all favorable to Lite-On’s content 
opportunity. However, project timing, customer qualifications and share shifts can have 
a greater effect on Lite-On than on a more diversified supplier such as Delta.
Mix and leverage should support a second leg of margin improvement
Lite-On’s first margin expansion came from restructuring and exiting lower-return 
businesses. We believe the next phase can be driven increasingly by product mix and 
operating leverage. Cloud & AIoT already represented approximately 55% of 2Q26 sales 
and should continue to increase as AI server power ramps. We forecast revenue rising to 
c.NT$219bn in 2026, NT$300bn in 2027 and NT$360bn+ in 2028, while gross margin 
remains in the mid-to-high 20s and operating margin expands as higher-value AI power 
products scale. Our EPS forecasts rise to approximately NT$10.9/NT$16.0/NT$20.0 in 
2026–28E. The key debate, in our view, is therefore moving from whether Lite-On can 
participate in AI power to whether it can sustain customer wins, execute a large capacity 
build and convert rapid sales growth into the margin profile implied by our forecasts.

Rising power density and AI buildout expand power TAM
The AI power opportunity is being driven by a fundamental increase in compute and 
power density at every level of the system. Accelerator package power rises as vendors 
integrate more compute dies and memory around each package; accelerator counts and 
scale-up bandwidth increase at the rack level; and the resulting rack moves from tens of 
kilowatts toward hundreds of kilowatts and ultimately megawatt-class designs.
Our companion AI Power analysis demonstrates why physical rack counts increasingly 
become the wrong denominator. From 2025 to 2030 we forecast AI server rack units 
increasing at only around a 12% CAGR, but average rack/system power at roughly 
39%, producing a 55% CAGR in annual IT GW deployed. Power-system content per 
watt adds another approximately 9% CAGR.
Together these variables drive our AI server power TAM from approximately US$6.6bn in 
2025 to US$91.1bn in 2030.

 Power conversion is becoming larger, shared and increasingly system-
level
The linear relationship between compute density and power load has hit what we call 
the "Amperage Wall" as AI accelerators transition from the "server era" — discrete 
units consuming 500–1,000W — to the "AI Factory era," defined by rack-scale systems 
consuming 120–140kW. We see three structural challenges that make a fundamental 
redesign of power architecture increasingly unavoidable: 
1. Current scales faster than power loss can be managed. As the current increases, 
resistive losses and heat generation rise exponentially.
2. Rising compute density leaves ever less physical space for power. The pursuit of 
higher compute density results in a massive thermal design power (TDP) load per 
rack, with the IT rack already packed with GPUs and cooling component, leaving 
little room for additional power-delivery system which encouraging the migration 
of power electronics into a dedicated sidecar power rack. 
3. Synchronized GPU cluster create severe transient load spike. AI training workloads 
are highly synchronized. Thousands of GPUs/AI ASICs can shift simultaneously 
between utilization states, creating instantaneous spikes in power consumption 
within milliseconds. 
We believe the industry is undergoing a structural changes with the 4 phases of data 
center architecture evolution (Figure 5A I  p o w e r  d e l i v e r y  e v o l v e s  f r o m  s e r v e r  P S U s  t o w a r d  c e n t r a l i z e d  s h e l v e s  a n d  d e d i c a t e d  p o w e r  r a c k s), AI power delivery is moving through a multi-
stage transition rather than changing from today’s 54V racks to native 800V in one step. 
Lite-On therefore has several avenues to participate before widespread native 800V 
adoption. Its addressable content includes PSUs, power shelves, controllers, BBU/energy 
storage, protection, rack hardware and DC/DC products. Over time, dedicated power 
racks add further system-integration opportunity.

0.13. As installed capacity rises with higher IT rack TDP , overall power content per 
PSU could increase by ~80%. 
2. Power shelves: The power shelf hosts the PSU module and PMU, taking facility 
AC input and outputting +/-400V or 800V DC. System integrators such as Lite-On 
typically supply the chassis, backplane, and cooling system, increasing captured 
content value. 
3. Battery Backup System: BBUs are designed to bridge sudden power failures, 
providing up to 45 seconds of runtime during AC loss before generators start. 

Supercapacitors offer an alternative, addressing millisecond-scale load transients 
via ramp-rate control and smoothing GPU power fluctuations. 
4. DC/DC convertor: While the power rack delivers HVDC to the IT rack, additional 
Phase 2 IT rack shelves step down high voltage to the lower voltage required by 
compute nodes. Current versions convert 800V to 54V, with potential to move 
further to 6V before compute nodes can be HV native fed.

Energy storage adds content, but architecture determines where that value sits
For Lite-On, BBU and CBU is both an opportunity and an architectural swing factor. 
Today, high BBU attachment on some hyperscale platforms materially increases content 
per rack. Our industry work estimates the combined BBU/CBU market grows 
substantially faster than the broader server-power market as AI load density rises.Longer 
term, pooled LFP UPS/BESS architectures could shift some battery value away from 
individual IT or power racks, but power-electronics demand should remain, given 
requirements for battery management, bidirectional conversion, controls, protection, 
and DC distribution. Suppliers with broader system-level capabilities may capture more 
value than vendors limited to standalone rack-level battery modules. 
Power Racks: ASIC provides the first tangible ramp, ahead of NVIDIA
Our Power TAM work suggests NVIDIA’s initial shift to dedicated power racks may be 
slower than expected. Vera Rubin/Oberon systems at ~225–230kW can still be 
supported by several hundred kilowatts of installed 54V rack-level shelf capacity, 
reducing near-term urgency to externalize conversion and giving operators more time to 
qualify high-voltage infrastructure and safety standards.
This is not seen as particularly negative for the overall Lite-On thesis. The bulk of 2026–
27 growth in our model comes from increasing AI accelerator deployment, larger rack 
power, higher-capacity PSUs and shelves, BBUs and richer ASIC systems—not from 
widespread native 800V adoption. 
Our feedback suggests Lite-On should begin ramping dedicated power racks at its top 
ASIC customer from late 2026, We expect the initial architecture to remain 48V, with 

~255kW of PSU capacity and ~170kW of BBU capacity supporting a 72-ASIC system. 
Despite remaining at 48V, moving power conversion and backup power into a dedicated 
rack materially increases Lite-On’s content, which we estimate rises from ~US$54k for 
the comparable rack-level architecture to ~US$117k per power rack, with content/W 
increasing from ~US$0.75 to ~US$0.98.
The larger step is expected with Amazon's 4th Gen system, which we believe will launch 
in late 2027. Based on multiple industry supply-chain conversations, we understand 
Amazon is targeting an ~800V architecture and materially higher rack power. Our 
expectation is driven in part by feedback suggesting a transition from the current 2-die 
chipset configuration to a higher-power 4-die design. Lite-On has been developing an 
approximately 1.2MW power rack capable of supporting two IT racks, which could lift 
system content to ~US$306k at roughly US$0.93/W. 
Importantly, this means slower near-term adoption of dedicated power racks on NVIDIA 
does not invalidate the opportunity. Trainium provides a tangible path to 
commercialization first, while NVIDIA, other ASIC platforms and ultimately 800V 
architectures broaden the addressable market thereafter.

Financial outlook: Cloud power drives a 
larger, more profitable earnings base
Lite-On is entering the next phase of its business transformation: portfolio restructuring 
has improved the underlying margin base, while the expansion of cloud power now 
provides the catalyst for revenue and earnings growth. Earlier disposals reduced 
exposure to lower-return businesses; the next stage depends on scaling customer 
programs, increasing power content supplied per deployment and converting the 
growing cloud mix into operating leverage. Our forecasts are principally driven by cloud 
power, with more moderate growth in optoelectronics and IT/consumer applications. 
We forecast revenue rising from NT$166.1bn in 2025 to NT$218.1bn in 2026, NT
$299.8bn in 2027 and NT$373.6bn in 2028—growth of 31%, 38% and 25%, 
respectively. Gross margin expands from 22.9% in 2025 to 25.2%/26.4%/26.6% in 
2026–28, while operating margin increases from 10.1% to 13.5%/15.3%/15.5%. This 
supports EPS of NT$10.85/NT$16.00/NT$20.00, representing approximately 44% 
compound annual growth over 2025–28 versus 31% revenue growth. We view the 
earnings opportunity therefore as not just a larger addressable market, but a greater 
proportion of revenue coming from higher-value power products. 
Importantly, the margin forecast does not extrapolate the exceptional 27.2% gross 
margin achieved in 2Q26. We model a more measured improvement as cloud products 
scale, allowing for continued engineering investment, capacity expansion and the costs 
of introducing new systems. The key execution test is whether Lite-On can translate 
qualifications and customer demand into repeatable volume production while 
maintaining pricing discipline and manufacturing efficiency.

Lite-On revenue model builds up the key drivers by product
Our revenue forecast is built by product and business line: Within cloud, we model 
power supplies and power shelves, BBUs, cooling, rack-related hardware and other 
products, alongside the AIoT/connectivity business. Power supplies and shelves remain 
the largest revenue contributor, while storage and the expansion into broader system 
content provide additional growth. Cooling and rack products broaden the opportunity 
without needing to become the principal earnings drivers in the near term. We forecast 
the cloud subtotal rising from approximately NT$60.5bn in 2025 to NT$105.5bn in 
2026, NT$176.0bn in 2027 and NT$242.1bn in 2028. Including AIoT, segment revenue 
increases from NT$75.1bn to NT$123.5bn/NT$195.8bn/NT$262.7bn, lifting its share of 
total revenue from approximately 45% in 2025 to 57%/65%/70%. 
This distinction matters for the investment case: legacy businesses do not need to shrink 
for the portfolio to improve. Faster cloud growth improves mix, while higher-value 
products and operating efficiency increase the earnings contribution from that mix.

Margins improved on divestment; Server mix drives the next upgrade
Lite-On’s margin expansion began in 2018, following the divestiture of its casing and 
camera module businesses, and subsequently its image BU and SSD businesses in later 
years. These actions lifted the company’s gross margin from the mid-teens to 
approximately 20% in 2021. We believe the next stage is different. Rather than relying 
primarily on further divestments, margin expansion should increasingly come from 
richer product mix, scale and operating leverage. Higher-power AI products are not 
simply larger versions of commodity PC PSUs. Moving from roughly 5.5kW modules 
toward 18kW+ modules requires higher power density, three-phase input, more 
demanding thermal management, dynamic response, redundancy, telemetry and 
system coordination. Power shelves, BBUs and rack-level systems add further control, 
protection and integration content.

Lite-On Q226 sales +21% QoQ, +30% YoY to NT$52.7bn with gross margin expanded

We expect H2'26 growth to be driven by a strong ASIC server ramp, bringing Q3 sales to

YoY in H2'26. We expect the LEO business to grow from a low base, doubling YoY in

has not seen material shortages or component pricing pressure affecting its core

Key risks to our investment thesis
 The principal risk is a slower AI infrastructure deployment cycle. Our industry work shows 
deployed IT GW is the single largest determinant of the power TAM, so a meaningful reduction in 
hyperscaler accelerator deployment would affect all power suppliers.
 Customer concentration is a second risk, particularly Lite-On’s large custom-ASIC exposure 
and reliance on a relatively small number of hyperscalers. Program delays or share changes can 
materially affect annual revenue.
 Execution on capacity expansion also matters. Lite-On is investing substantially ahead of 
forecast demand; if utilization ramps more slowly, depreciation and fixed operating costs could 
limit expected margin improvement.
 Competitive pricing remains a risk as more suppliers qualify for high-power products. 
We believe the move toward larger, more engineered modules and systems should moderate 
pure commodity pricing pressure, but it will not eliminate it.
 Architecture is another source of uncertainty. A slower transition to external power racks is 
not particularly damaging to our near-term thesis because 48/54V systems still require 
substantial power content. Longer term, however, the precise mix between rack-level BBUs, 
pooled UPS/BESS, ±400V, single-bus 800V and facility-level conversion will determine where 
value accrues within the supply chain.
 Rising competition and slower spec upgrades would impact earnings. Faster progress 
from Chinese power suppliers, FX movements and weaker legacy IT/consumer demand could 
create additional earnings variability.

Company Description
Founded in 1975, Lite-On Technology is Taiwan's first listed electronics company and a global 
leader in power management and optoelectronic solutions. Originally a pioneer in LED 
technologies, the company has evolved into a key supplier of AI infrastructure, cloud 
computing, automotive electronics, 5G and AIoT solutions.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Lite-On Technology using PE methodology. Key risks to our investment thesis:
The principal risk is a slower AI infrastructure deployment cycle. Our industry work shows 
deployed IT GW is the single-largest determinant of the power TAM, so a meaningful 
reduction in hyperscaler accelerator deployment would affect all power suppliers.
Customer concentration is a second risk, particularly Lite-On’s large custom-ASIC exposure 
and reliance on a relatively small number of hyperscalers. Program delays or share changes 
can materially affect annual revenue.
Execution on capacity expansion also matters. Lite-On is investing substantially ahead of 
forecast demand; if utilization ramps more slowly, depreciation and fixed operating costs 
could limit expected margin improvement.
Competitive pricing remains a risk as more suppliers qualify for high-power products. We 
believe the move toward larger, more engineered modules and systems should moderate 
pure commodity pricing pressure, but it will not eliminate it.
Architecture is another source of uncertainty. A slower transition to external power racks is 
not particularly damaging to our near-term thesis because 48/54V systems still require 
substantial power content. Longer term, however, the precise mix between rack-level BBUs, 
pooled UPS/BESS, ±400V, single-bus 800V and facility-level conversion will determine where 
value accrues within the supply chain.
Rising competition and slower spec upgrades would impact earnings. Faster progress from 
Chinese power suppliers, FX movements and weaker legacy IT/consumer demand could 
create additional earnings variability.
HOLT methodology
The HOLT methodology does not assign ratings or a target price to a security. It is an analytical 
tool that involves use of a set of proprietary quantitative algorithms and warranted value 
calculations, collectively called the HOLT valuation model, that are consistently applied to all 
the companies included in its database. The HOLT valuation model is a discounted cash flow 
model. Third-party data (including consensus earnings estimates) are systematically translated 
into a number of default variables and incorporated into the algorithms available in the HOLT 
valuation model. The source financial statement, pricing, and earnings data provided by 
outside data vendors are subject to quality control and may also be adjusted to more closely 
measure the underlying economics of firm performance. These adjustments provide 
consistency when analyzing a single company across time, or analyzing multiple companies 
across industries or national borders. The default scenario that is produced by the HOLT 
valuation model establishes a warranted price that represents the expected mean value for a 
security based upon empirically derived fade algorithms that forecast a firm's future return on 
capital and growth rates over an extended period of time. As the third-party data are 
updated, the warranted price updates automatically. A company’s future achieved return on 
capital or growth rate may differ from HOLT default forecast. Additional information about 
the HOLT methodology is available upon request.

(emoji)UBS_光寶科(2301, Initiate at Buy, TP$400)

(emoji)公司是台灣電力電子供應商，業務涵蓋雲端電源、光電及車用領域，目前持續提高AI伺服器電源布局。認為隨著執行力改善、客戶基礎擴大及毛利率提升，公司有望更充分掌握AI電源電子市場的成長機會。

(emoji)雲端電源預計占2026年營收48%，將受惠於AI硬體部署規模擴大及單位功率中的產品價值提升，AI電源市場預估至2030年將以69%年複合成長率擴大至912億美元，並受400V及800V直流架構轉型帶動，因此預期公司營收及獲利將優於市場共識。

(emoji)公司雖屬較晚進入市場的業者，但近期動能明顯提升，已取得NVIDIA認證供應商資格，並供應前五大CSP中的三家，同時在其中一家ASIC伺服器的電源供應具領先地位。預期首款專用48V ASIC電源機櫃將於2026年底開始放量，2027年底起則進一步轉向產品價值更高的800V/MW級架構，並預期未來12至18個月內打入另外兩家超大規模雲端業者。

(emoji)Cloud與AIoT營收成長已由2024年的年減2%，加速至2025年的年增48%及2026年至今的60%，主要受設計案持續放量帶動，搭配更聚焦的策略、研發投入及資產負債表支持，有助公司維持資料中心白區電源前三大地位並掌握AI成長。

(emoji)公司近年已將產品組合重新調整至高成長、高毛利市場，處分部分業務後，集團毛利率已由2021年的中高個位數提升至約20%，預期AI將帶動下一階段毛利率擴張，隨AI業務占比提高，2026至2027年毛利率有望加速提升至27至29%。其中Cloud與AIoT營業利益率約20%，明顯高於光電的9%及IT/CE的7.5%，顯示產品組合改善仍有進一步空間，加上伺服器業務效率提升及維持營收5至6%的研發投入，營業利益率亦有望改善。

(emoji)估2026/2027/2028年EPS 10.85/16.00/20.00元。

Initiation of Coverage
Lite-On Technology
A stronger contender in AI power
Lite-On better positioned to capture AI growth; Initiate at Buy, PT NT$400
Lite-On is a Taiwan-based power electronics supplier spanning cloud power,
optoelectronics and auto, increasingly focused on AI server power. We expect Lite-On to
capture more of the expanding AI power electronics opportunity as execution improves,
its customer base broadens and margins rise. Cloud power (48% of our 2026 sales
forecast) should benefit from higher content per watt alongside growth in GW of AI
hardware deployed. We forecast the AI power TAM to grow at a 69% CAGR to US
$91.2bn in 2030 (link), supported by transitions to 400/800V DC architectures. These
drivers underpin our above-consensus sales and earnings forecasts. We initiate coverage
with a Buy rating and NT$400 target, implying 20x 2028E EPS versus peers at 22x.
Late entrant gaining momentum; ASICs open up its power-rack opportunity
Lite-On has improved execution, securing NVIDIA approved-vendor qualification and
supplying three of the top five CSPs, with a leading position in power supplies for one of
the ASIC servers. Our checks point to a first dedicated 48V ASIC power rack ramp from
late 2026, followed by a substantially higher-content 800V/MW-class architecture with
the next generation from late 2027. We expect penetration into the remaining two
hyperscalers within 12-18 months. Cloud & AIoT revenue growth accelerated from -2%
in 2024 to +48% in 2025 and +60% in 2026 YTD as design wins scaled. Stronger focus,
R&D investment and balance sheet support should help Lite-On sustain a top-three
position in data-centre white-space power and capture AI-driven growth.
Portfolio repositioning sets up the next phase of margin expansion
Lite-On has restructured its portfolio toward higher-growth, higher-margin markets.
Divestitures lifted group gross margin from the mid-teens to approximately 20% in
2021. We expect AI to drive the next phase of expansion, with Delta’s AI ramp
illustrating the potential benefits from a richer product mix and operating leverage. Lite-
On’s margin expansion should accelerate in 2026-27 as AI exposure increases, with
gross margin potentially reaching 27-29%. Cloud & AIoT OpM of 20%, vs. 9% for Opto
and 7.5% for IT/CE, highlight the opportunity for further mix improvement. Greater
operating efficiency in the server business should also support operating margins, while
R&D spending remains at 5-6% of sales.
Valuation: AI growth supports a higher trading multiple
Our NT$400 price target applies 20x to our 2028E EPS of NT$20, equivalent to 25x our
2027E EPS of NT$16 versus peers at 29x. Lite-On has historically traded at 8-14x P/E, but
we believe its transition into a key AI power supplier warrants a higher multiple. Our
EPS grows at a 43% CAGR to NT$20 from 2025-2028E (vs. 57% for Delta) from the
combination of AI revenue growth and margin expansion, supporting the case for
further re-rating. Growth is supported by higher capex at NT$18bn in 2026 (vs. NT
$4.6bn past 3 yrs avg.) to more than double its capacity by the end of 2026.

Q: Can Lite-On better participate in the industry's strong AI power electronics growth?
After lagging early in the AI cycle, Lite-On has improved execution, securing NVIDIA qualification and
supplying 3 of the top 5 CSPs, including leading on Trainium servers and targeting shipments to the
other top 2 hyperscalers in the next 12-18 months. Cloud & AIoT growth accelerated from -2% YoY
in 2024 to +48%/+60% in 2025/'26 YTD, supported by design wins, R&D, and capacity expansion.
Lite-On can remain a top-three white-space supplier as AI TAM grows. However, Delta Electronics
(2308.TW) should retain ~50% share given incumbency, R&D, technical support, and ecosystem ties.
Q: Is Lite-On able to further improve its margins?
Lite-On gross margin has improved from 17% in 2020 to 23% in 2025, with OpM rising from 6% to
10%. We view this as largely self-help, trimming the legacy low-margin business, with the payoff
from AI product only beginning to show. We expect GM can further improve to above 25% while
OpM stays at 15-18% as AI exposure rises and the company becomes more vertically integrated,
moving from a component supplier toward a system integrator.
Q: Would the mature business drag on Lite-On's operations?
We see the mature business as less important to growth rather than becoming a material drag on
group earnings as Opto-electronic BU and traditional power supply BU lowers from 55% of 2025
sales to 43%/35% of 2026-27 sales. We also view this business growing single digits YoY as it offsets
mature growth in PC/game console with growth into LEO (3% of sales but doubling YoY), industrial
IoT for its optocouplers and LED into more Auto/EV applications and tuck-in acquisitions. The
business is also a cash cow so on mild growth can maintain high-single-digit OpM.
We expect Lite-On to benefit from AI power electronics TAM expansion and margin improvement as
execution, market penetration, and customer diversification improve. Cloud power, representing
48% of 2026 sales, should drive strong growth through content/W expansion and healthy growth in
GW hardware deployments. These factors should support earnings growth above Street
expectations. We initiate with a Buy rating and NT$400 target, based on 20x 2028E EPS.
Our bottom-up analysis of AI capex and supply chain inputs across ODMs, foundry, back-end,
memory, and fabless/design services, plus rack upgrades for higher TDP , supports a strong power
industry TAM outlook. At OCP APAC 2026, Lite-On showcased a full 1MW TDP rack solution after Q3
shipments of a lower-spec power rack solution to an ASIC vender, underscoring its shift from
component supplier to system integrator. We expect the AI power market to grow at a 69% CAGR in
2025-30, with Lite-On among the top-three suppliers and gaining share faster than the industry.
The stock has rallied +66% YTD with the market re-rating it  as part of the AI supply chain on its solid
results +21.4% QoQ in Q226 as evidence. The stock now trades at 22x next-12-month consensus PE,
above its historical range of 8-14x. However, we believe further upside exists supported by our global
TAM growth and Lite-On's traction improved to captured the industry growth.

Executive Summary
We initiate coverage of Lite-On Technology with a Buy rating and NT$400 price target,
based on 20x our 2028E EPS of NT$20.0, or approximately 25x our 2027E EPS of NT
$16.0. The stock has already re-rated materially as investors recognize its improving
participation in AI power, but we believe the change in the earnings base is structural.
Lite-On has spent several years exiting lower-return businesses, improving its margin
structure and redirecting investment toward Cloud & AIoT, where AI server power is now
becoming a meaningful growth and earnings driver. Our target multiple remains below
the roughly 22x level at which the broader power-supply peer group trades, reflecting
Lite-On’s later entry and still-developing customer breadth. We forecast revenue growth
of 31%/38%/25% in 2026/27/28 and EPS growth of 63%/47%/25%, supported by a
rising cloud mix and operating leverage.
Lite-On is moving from proving participation to scaling in AI power
The core change in our thesis is that Lite-On no longer needs to prove that it can enter AI
server power; it increasingly needs to demonstrate how far it can scale. AI server PSU
shipments began ramping in late 2024/2025, customer qualifications have broadened,
and the company is moving beyond individual power modules into larger power shelves,
BBU/energy-management systems and eventually dedicated high-voltage power racks.
Importantly, our checks suggest the power-rack opportunity is already becoming
tangible on custom ASICs: we expect Lite-On to begin ramping a dedicated 48V power
rack for its top ASIC client from late 2026, before stepping up to an ~800V/MW-class
architecture with the following generation from late 2027. Lite-On remains well behind
Delta in absolute AI power scale and breadth, but our forecasts do not require it to close
that gap. The base case assumes only modest GPU-server share and stronger positions in
selected custom-ASIC programs, leaving additional CSP wins as potential upside rather
than a prerequisite.
AI power growth is a watts story, not an 800V adoption call
Our companion AI Power report (link) estimates industry AI server power-electronics
TAM rising from approximately US$6.6bn in 2025 to US$91.1bn in 2030, a 69% CAGR.
AI server rack shipments grow only around 12% CAGR in our model; the much larger
drivers are a roughly 39% CAGR in average rack power and 55% CAGR in annual IT GW
deployed, supplemented by higher power-system content per watt. This distinction
matters for Lite-On. We expect strong 2026–27 AI power growth even if NVIDIA’s initial
transition to dedicated 800V power racks is slower than previously expected. Higher
accelerator shipments, the transition at its top ASIC customer to a richer 48V followed
by 800V power rack, AMD’s move toward rack-scale systems and increasing custom-
ASIC rack density should drive substantial growth before widespread native 800V
adoption, which should start with its ASIC customer from late 2027. The 400/800V
transition becomes a more meaningful incremental content opportunity from 2028
onward rather than the foundation of our near-term estimates.
ASIC exposure is a differentiator, while concentration is a risk
Lite-On is largely exposed to custom-ASIC power relative to the industry. We estimate
ASIC programs contribute roughly two-thirds of its modeled AI power exposure over
much of our forecast period, compared with custom ASICs representing roughly 40–
50% of industry AI power TAM. This creates both opportunity and concentration risk.
ASIC systems are moving toward more accelerators per rack, higher BBU attachment
and increasingly rack-level power architectures, all favorable to Lite-On’s content
opportunity. However, project timing, customer qualifications and share shifts can have
a greater effect on Lite-On than on a more diversified supplier such as Delta.
Mix and leverage should support a second leg of margin improvement
Lite-On’s first margin expansion came from restructuring and exiting lower-return
businesses. We believe the next phase can be driven increasingly by product mix and
operating leverage. Cloud & AIoT already represented approximately 55% of 2Q26 sales
and should continue to increase as AI server power ramps. We forecast revenue rising to
c.NT$219bn in 2026, NT$300bn in 2027 and NT$360bn+ in 2028, while gross margin
remains in the mid-to-high 20s and operating margin expands as higher-value AI power
products scale. Our EPS forecasts rise to approximately NT$10.9/NT$16.0/NT$20.0 in
2026–28E. The key debate, in our view, is therefore moving from whether Lite-On can
participate in AI power to whether it can sustain customer wins, execute a large capacity
build and convert rapid sales growth into the margin profile implied by our forecasts.

Rising power density and AI buildout expand power TAM
The AI power opportunity is being driven by a fundamental increase in compute and
power density at every level of the system. Accelerator package power rises as vendors
integrate more compute dies and memory around each package; accelerator counts and
scale-up bandwidth increase at the rack level; and the resulting rack moves from tens of
kilowatts toward hundreds of kilowatts and ultimately megawatt-class designs.
Our companion AI Power analysis demonstrates why physical rack counts increasingly
become the wrong denominator. From 2025 to 2030 we forecast AI server rack units
increasing at only around a 12% CAGR, but average rack/system power at roughly
39%, producing a 55% CAGR in annual IT GW deployed. Power-system content per
watt adds another approximately 9% CAGR.
Together these variables drive our AI server power TAM from approximately US$6.6bn in
2025 to US$91.1bn in 2030.

 Power conversion is becoming larger, shared and increasingly system-
level
The linear relationship between compute density and power load has hit what we call
the "Amperage Wall" as AI accelerators transition from the "server era" — discrete
units consuming 500–1,000W — to the "AI Factory era," defined by rack-scale systems
consuming 120–140kW. We see three structural challenges that make a fundamental
redesign of power architecture increasingly unavoidable:
1. Current scales faster than power loss can be managed. As the current increases,
resistive losses and heat generation rise exponentially.
2. Rising compute density leaves ever less physical space for power. The pursuit of
higher compute density results in a massive thermal design power (TDP) load per
rack, with the IT rack already packed with GPUs and cooling component, leaving
little room for additional power-delivery system which encouraging the migration
of power electronics into a dedicated sidecar power rack.
3. Synchronized GPU cluster create severe transient load spike. AI training workloads
are highly synchronized. Thousands of GPUs/AI ASICs can shift simultaneously
between utilization states, creating instantaneous spikes in power consumption
within milliseconds.
We believe the industry is undergoing a structural changes with the 4 phases of data
center architecture evolution (Figure 5A I  p o w e r  d e l i v e r y  e v o l v e s  f r o m  s e r v e r  P S U s  t o w a r d  c e n t r a l i z e d  s h e l v e s  a n d  d e d i c a t e d  p o w e r  r a c k s), AI power delivery is moving through a multi-
stage transition rather than changing from today’s 54V racks to native 800V in one step.
Lite-On therefore has several avenues to participate before widespread native 800V
adoption. Its addressable content includes PSUs, power shelves, controllers, BBU/energy
storage, protection, rack hardware and DC/DC products. Over time, dedicated power
racks add further system-integration opportunity.

Energy storage adds content, but architecture determines where that value sits
For Lite-On, BBU and CBU is both an opportunity and an architectural swing factor.
Today, high BBU attachment on some hyperscale platforms materially increases content
per rack. Our industry work estimates the combined BBU/CBU market grows
substantially faster than the broader server-power market as AI load density rises.Longer
term, pooled LFP UPS/BESS architectures could shift some battery value away from
individual IT or power racks, but power-electronics demand should remain, given
requirements for battery management, bidirectional conversion, controls, protection,
and DC distribution. Suppliers with broader system-level capabilities may capture more
value than vendors limited to standalone rack-level battery modules.
Power Racks: ASIC provides the first tangible ramp, ahead of NVIDIA
Our Power TAM work suggests NVIDIA’s initial shift to dedicated power racks may be
slower than expected. Vera Rubin/Oberon systems at ~225–230kW can still be
supported by several hundred kilowatts of installed 54V rack-level shelf capacity,
reducing near-term urgency to externalize conversion and giving operators more time to
qualify high-voltage infrastructure and safety standards.
This is not seen as particularly negative for the overall Lite-On thesis. The bulk of 2026–
27 growth in our model comes from increasing AI accelerator deployment, larger rack
power, higher-capacity PSUs and shelves, BBUs and richer ASIC systems—not from
widespread native 800V adoption.
Our feedback suggests Lite-On should begin ramping dedicated power racks at its top
ASIC customer from late 2026, We expect the initial architecture to remain 48V, with

~255kW of PSU capacity and ~170kW of BBU capacity supporting a 72-ASIC system.
Despite remaining at 48V, moving power conversion and backup power into a dedicated
rack materially increases Lite-On’s content, which we estimate rises from ~US$54k for
the comparable rack-level architecture to ~US$117k per power rack, with content/W
increasing from ~US$0.75 to ~US$0.98.
The larger step is expected with Amazon's 4th Gen system, which we believe will launch
in late 2027. Based on multiple industry supply-chain conversations, we understand
Amazon is targeting an ~800V architecture and materially higher rack power. Our
expectation is driven in part by feedback suggesting a transition from the current 2-die
chipset configuration to a higher-power 4-die design. Lite-On has been developing an
approximately 1.2MW power rack capable of supporting two IT racks, which could lift
system content to ~US$306k at roughly US$0.93/W.
Importantly, this means slower near-term adoption of dedicated power racks on NVIDIA
does not invalidate the opportunity. Trainium provides a tangible path to
commercialization first, while NVIDIA, other ASIC platforms and ultimately 800V
architectures broaden the addressable market thereafter.

Beyond the Trainium ramp, two main platforms should drive power rack adoption:
1. OCP's Mount Diablo platform was the first widely adopted open-standard
implementation, initially targeting approximately 72kW of power-rack capacity.
Based on our industry feedback, the power rack is in the qualification stage right
now with the sample rack shipping in Q4 and mass production in H127.
2. NVIDIA's own reference architecture is materially more aggressive, centered
around a 660kW power-rack design incorporating six 110kW rectifier shelves and
480kW of battery backup capacity. While OCP introduced the architecture earlier
to establish an open ecosystem and accelerate adoption, NVIDIA's higher-power
implementation is designed for the next generation Rubin Ultra, given that the
current power shelves design can still support the Vera Rubin generation.
We think industry concerns over NVIDIA’s 2027 power rack implementation delays
should have a limited impact on Lite-On, given its stronger relative position in ASIC. We
expect robust growth, supported by strong GW of compute deployments and healthy
~60% power upgrades on the VR200 platform. Our sensitivity analysis indicates NVIDIA
power-rack penetration has only a mode

Financial outlook: Cloud power drives a
larger, more profitable earnings base
Lite-On is entering the next phase of its business transformation: portfolio restructuring
has improved the underlying margin base, while the expansion of cloud power now
provides the catalyst for revenue and earnings growth. Earlier disposals reduced
exposure to lower-return businesses; the next stage depends on scaling customer
programs, increasing power content supplied per deployment and converting the
growing cloud mix into operating leverage. Our forecasts are principally driven by cloud
power, with more moderate growth in optoelectronics and IT/consumer applications.
We forecast revenue rising from NT$166.1bn in 2025 to NT$218.1bn in 2026, NT
$299.8bn in 2027 and NT$373.6bn in 2028—growth of 31%, 38% and 25%,
respectively. Gross margin expands from 22.9% in 2025 to 25.2%/26.4%/26.6% in
2026–28, while operating margin increases from 10.1% to 13.5%/15.3%/15.5%. This
supports EPS of NT$10.85/NT$16.00/NT$20.00, representing approximately 44%
compound annual growth over 2025–28 versus 31% revenue growth. We view the
earnings opportunity therefore as not just a larger addressable market, but a greater
proportion of revenue coming from higher-value power products.
Importantly, the margin forecast does not extrapolate the exceptional 27.2% gross
margin achieved in 2Q26. We model a more measured improvement as cloud products
scale, allowing for continued engineering investment, capacity expansion and the costs
of introducing new systems. The key execution test is whether Lite-On can translate
qualifications and customer demand into repeatable volume production while
maintaining pricing discipline and manufacturing efficiency.

Lite-On revenue model builds up the key drivers by product
Our revenue forecast is built by product and business line: Within cloud, we model
power supplies and power shelves, BBUs, cooling, rack-related hardware and other
products, alongside the AIoT/connectivity business. Power supplies and shelves remain
the largest revenue contributor, while storage and the expansion into broader system
content provide additional growth. Cooling and rack products broaden the opportunity
without needing to become the principal earnings drivers in the near term. We forecast
the cloud subtotal rising from approximately NT$60.5bn in 2025 to NT$105.5bn in
2026, NT$176.0bn in 2027 and NT$242.1bn in 2028. Including AIoT, segment revenue
increases from NT$75.1bn to NT$123.5bn/NT$195.8bn/NT$262.7bn, lifting its share of
total revenue from approximately 45% in 2025 to 57%/65%/70%.
This distinction matters for the investment case: legacy businesses do not need to shrink
for the portfolio to improve. Faster cloud growth improves mix, while higher-value
products and operating efficiency increase the earnings contribution from that mix.

Margins improved on divestment; Server mix drives the next upgrade
Lite-On’s margin expansion began in 2018, following the divestiture of its casing and
camera module businesses, and subsequently its image BU and SSD businesses in later
years. These actions lifted the company’s gross margin from the mid-teens to
approximately 20% in 2021. We believe the next stage is different. Rather than relying
primarily on further divestments, margin expansion should increasingly come from
richer product mix, scale and operating leverage. Higher-power AI products are not
simply larger versions of commodity PC PSUs. Moving from roughly 5.5kW modules
toward 18kW+ modules requires higher power density, three-phase input, more
demanding thermal management, dynamic response, redundancy, telemetry and
system coordination. Power shelves, BBUs and rack-level systems add further control,
protection and integration content.

Q2 results inflected with stronger participation in the DC growth trend
Lite-On Q226 sales +21% QoQ, +30% YoY to NT$52.7bn with gross margin expanded

H226 growth momentum should continue with 2027 ramp.
We expect H2'26 growth to be driven by a strong ASIC server ramp, bringing Q3 sales to
+10.5% QoQ and full-year sales to +31.3% YoY, to NT$218bn. The next-generation
8.5kW PSU should ship with BBUs at a 1:1 ratio, driven by Trainium 3, while the 800VDC
rack supporting the GPU platform should complete qualification in Q4, with small-
volume shipments in late 2026 — bringing Cloud & AIoT growth to 43% HoH / 79%
YoY in H2'26. We expect the LEO business to grow from a low base, doubling YoY in

has not seen material shortages or component pricing pressure affecting its core

Key risks to our investment thesis
 The principal risk is a slower AI infrastructure deployment cycle. Our industry work shows
deployed IT GW is the single largest determinant of the power TAM, so a meaningful reduction in
hyperscaler accelerator deployment would affect all power suppliers.
 Customer concentration is a second risk, particularly Lite-On’s large custom-ASIC exposure
and reliance on a relatively small number of hyperscalers. Program delays or share changes can
materially affect annual revenue.
 Execution on capacity expansion also matters. Lite-On is investing substantially ahead of
forecast demand; if utilization ramps more slowly, depreciation and fixed operating costs could
limit expected margin improvement.
 Competitive pricing remains a risk as more suppliers qualify for high-power products.
We believe the move toward larger, more engineered modules and systems should moderate
pure commodity pricing pressure, but it will not eliminate it.
 Architecture is another source of uncertainty. A slower transition to external power racks is
not particularly damaging to our near-term thesis because 48/54V systems still require
substantial power content. Longer term, however, the precise mix between rack-level BBUs,
pooled UPS/BESS, ±400V, single-bus 800V and facility-level conversion will determine where
value accrues within the supply chain.
 Rising competition and slower spec upgrades would impact earnings. Faster progress
from Chinese power suppliers, FX movements and weaker legacy IT/consumer demand could
create additional earnings variability.

Company Description
Founded in 1975, Lite-On Technology is Taiwan's first listed electronics company and a global
leader in power management and optoelectronic solutions. Originally a pioneer in LED
technologies, the company has evolved into a key supplier of AI infrastructure, cloud
computing, automotive electronics, 5G and AIoT solutions.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Lite-On Technology using PE methodology. Key risks to our investment thesis:
The principal risk is a slower AI infrastructure deployment cycle. Our industry work shows
deployed IT GW is the single-largest determinant of the power TAM, so a meaningful
reduction in hyperscaler accelerator deployment would affect all power suppliers.
Customer concentration is a second risk, particularly Lite-On’s large custom-ASIC exposure
and reliance on a relatively small number of hyperscalers. Program delays or share changes
can materially affect annual revenue.
Execution on capacity expansion also matters. Lite-On is investing substantially ahead of
forecast demand; if utilization ramps more slowly, depreciation and fixed operating costs
could limit expected margin improvement.
Competitive pricing remains a risk as more suppliers qualify for high-power products. We
believe the move toward larger, more engineered modules and systems should moderate
pure commodity pricing pressure, but it will not eliminate it.
Architecture is another source of uncertainty. A slower transition to external power racks is
not particularly damaging to our near-term thesis because 48/54V systems still require
substantial power content. Longer term, however, the precise mix between rack-level BBUs,
pooled UPS/BESS, ±400V, single-bus 800V and facility-level conversion will determine where
value accrues within the supply chain.
Rising competition and slower spec upgrades would impact earnings. Faster progress from
Chinese power suppliers, FX movements and weaker legacy IT/consumer demand could
create additional earnings variability.
HOLT methodology

tool that involves use of a set of proprietary quantitative algorithms and warranted value
calculations, collectively called the HOLT valuation model, that are consistently applied to all
the companies included in its database. The HOLT valuation model is a discounted cash flow
model. Third-party data (including consensus earnings estimates) are systematically translated
into a number of default variables and incorporated into the algorithms available in the HOLT
valuation model. The source financial statement, pricing, and earnings data provided by
outside data vendors are subject to quality control and may also be adjusted to more closely
measure the underlying economics of firm performance. These adjustments provide
consistency when analyzing a single company across time, or analyzing multiple companies
across industries or national borders. The default scenario that is produced by the HOLT
valuation model establishes a warranted price that represents the expected mean value for a
security based upon empirically derived fade algorithms that forecast a firm's future return on
capital and growth rates over an extended period of time. As the third-party data are
updated, the warranted price updates automatically. A company’s future achieved return on
capital or growth rate may differ from HOLT default forecast. Additional information about

Summary

■ 台股
盤勢追蹤
4
近期焦點
9/7~9/11
美國數據與Fed追蹤：
• 美國8月PPI年增率5.4%，預期5.3%，前值4.8%。
• 財長貝森特宣布，將回購60億美元長天期政府債券，規模相當於一般操作的3倍，然規模未如預期。
• 美國8月CPI月增率從0.1%上升至0.4%，符合預期，為今年6月以來新高；8月核心CPI月增率0.3%，預期0.2%、前值0.2%。其中，無線通訊服務價格月增率達 5.9%，
對核心CPI月增率貢獻約0.1個百分點。
產業/企業動向：
• 媒體報導，美國政府近期與美國煉油商開會討論如何利用國防生產法擴大美國國內煉油產能 。煉油商表示，新建煉油廠需數年才能投入使用 ，傾向提高現有煉油廠
效率。
• 甲骨文盤後公佈FY1Q27 EPS 1.92 美元，預期1.67 美元，整體營收擊敗市場預期。其中雲端基礎設施營收年增率突破100%以上。
• 蘋果公司在秋季新品發表會推出自家首款折疊手機iPhone Duo。新機搭載台積電2奈米製程A20 Pro晶片，展開後螢幕尺寸達7.6吋，售價從1,999美元起跳。媒體報
導，OpenAI目前預計，到2030年算力支出將達到約7500億美元，目前OpenAI仍感覺算力非常不足。
國際市場與地緣政治情勢：
• 媒體報導，波斯灣國家外長計劃 9/14與伊朗外長會面，以討論荷莫茲海峽相關協議 。沙烏地阿拉伯繞過荷莫茲海峽的東西向輸油管遭襲擊後關閉 。媒體報導，美國
部署逾100名美軍顧問至沙烏地境內，支援沙國對抗葉門叛軍。葉門叛軍重申航行封鎖只針對沙國，直到沙國停止侵略、解除封鎖。
• 歐洲央行（ECB）如市場預期升息25bp至2.50%，拉加德稱三種情境下本次升息均經得起檢驗，並上調未來兩年通膨預期，暗示升息週期尚未結束。
台灣：
• 財政部公布8月出口達824億美元，月增9.4%、年增41%，創下歷年單月新高紀錄；台灣出口連續第34個月呈現正成長，追平史上最長紀錄。
• 台積電公布8 月營收，合併營收5,148 億 600 萬元，較 7 月增加 10.1％、年增大幅攀升 53.3％，創下單月歷史新高，並連續四個月改寫紀錄。
9/14~9/18 • FOMC會議、BoJ會議
通膨數據高於預期，蘋果發布會，後續關注美日利率決議
重點觀察及事件前瞻
6
通膨風險偏向上行，市場高度定價升息預期
■ 整體CPI符合預期，但核心通膨偏熱。其中，核心服務月增由0.2%加速至0.5%，顯示服務通膨仍具黏性。能源是整體CPI最大推力，能源價格
月增2.1%，其中汽油上漲3.9%，單一項目即貢獻約整體CPI漲幅的三分之一。
■ 核心通膨上升部分來自波動性項目，集中在核心服務項目，如：旅館住宿、機票、教育及通訊價格明顯上漲。其中，通訊費大幅走高，對核心
CPI約貢獻0.1個百分點，若排除該項目，核心CPI可能接近0.2%。核心商品月增則降至0.1%，顯示，關稅尚未造成全面性的商品通膨 。另一
方面，最具黏性的住房與部分醫療通膨並未重新失控，如：房租與屋主等值租金僅月增0.2%，醫療、汽車保險等價格下跌。
■ 債券建議以1～3年期美債及短存續期投資級公司債為主，長天期債券殖利率雖已具吸引力，但在油價未回落前不宜急於大幅拉長存續期間，可
採分批布局。美國期中選舉前市場波動風險仍存，維持輪動格局看法不變，優先布局金融、高股東回報及已展現AI變現能力的科技龍頭與軟體
應用股亦可逢回布局，建議避開高估值、依賴外部融資且財務體質較差的標的。隨著美股接近歷史新高，滿水位者可擇機調節漲多部位；半導
體相關的AI基礎設施則著眼中長線，逢回加碼。

焦點專題：台積電重新定義晶圓代工邊界
8
✓ 邏輯晶片：重視效能->功耗->面積，用於算力(增強GPU)
✓ DRAM/HBM：重視儲存密度/頻寬->良率->成本，用於餵飽算力(加速GPU記憶體供應系統)
封裝成為晶片設計與製程的延伸
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)
台積電/晶圓代工一線廠 三星、美光、海力士/記憶體廠
定位 先進邏輯晶片代工製造 記憶體製造，三星另有先進邏輯製造
主要產品 CPU、GPU、SoC、AI加速器等 DRAM、NAND、HBM
代表技術 FinFET(過去)、GAA、nanosheet、CoWoS HKMG、MR-MUF、TSV、4D NAND
製程優化方向 高效能、低功耗邏輯晶片，橫向拼合與立體化
(2.5D、3D)先進封裝 記憶體單元微縮化、高層數垂直堆疊
優勢來源 邏輯製程，積累IP、EDA、PDK及長期客戶生態
系
長期專注 DRAM / NAND，累積龐大的記憶體
製程、堆疊和量產經驗
AI時代關鍵 放入更多電晶體的同時降低功耗 提升HBM頻寬/能耗/穩定度
9
✓ 邏輯晶片與記憶體製程優化方向不同： 雖邏輯晶片與記憶體皆採 CMOS製程，但最佳化方向完全不同 ，
邏輯晶片重視電晶體強度(開關速度/是否漏電/密度/供電/高速互聯)，DRAM強調把位元做小，意即在極小
的平面面積中仍具有足夠電容 (深溝槽/高深寬比/位元線/儲存陣列)，而若走到NAND，則更重視在晶圓上
堆疊上百層存儲單元外，每一層皆可穩定正常運作(高深寬比蝕刻/薄膜沉積/溝道通孔/垂直堆疊/耐用度)
✓ 邏輯製程去做記憶體不具經濟效益： 即使邏輯製程可以做SRAM甚至整合SRAM+I/O+RF，但因需要優化
的部分不同，會浪費很多資金在不必要的方向 ，在成本考量上沒有經濟效益 ，且記憶體客戶希望節省每
個位元的單價 ，而邏輯客戶卻可以為了追求更高效能花更多錢 ，故兩者分開完成後再封裝更具成本優勢
。
邏輯晶片與記憶體製程優化方向不同
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)
邏輯晶片 記憶體
核心目標 高效能、低功耗 高密度、低成本、大容量
製程特色 複雜不規則的電路，有不同尺寸及用途的電晶體 大量重複規則的陣列，由極小的記憶體單元組成
強調重點 電晶體性能、互連效率、元件整合 記憶體單元面積、可靠度、良率
10
✓ 過去半導體製程中 ，電晶體微縮是首要目標 ，惟走到高速運算系統 ，先進封裝把邏輯晶片和記憶體
(HBM)拉入同一個系統 ，電晶體 、HBM、先進封裝皆會影響整個 AI系統的性能和良率 ，若能將 GPU和
HBM連接更快，則整體效能可進一步提升，故封裝地位顯著提升，成為各家鑽研的項目
✓ 當整個系統從單獨的 GPU和記憶體，變成GPU、HBM、CoWoS、先進互連等全部一起設計時 ，先進封
裝會侵蝕掉一部分原本由記憶體廠掌握的系統價值*，導致HBM價值可能被重新分配。參照台積電技術論
壇提出 、預計2028年開始量產的方案 ，計畫將 14倍光罩尺寸的 CoWoS整合10個大型運算晶粒與 20個
HBM堆疊
*Logic + CoWoS -> Logic + HBM + 3D stacking + advanced packaging
系統性整合時代來臨，記憶體價值部分被重新分配
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)

Interposer
11
✓ CoWoS為封裝價值提升的典範： CoWoS將多個GPU/ASIC與 HBM高密度整合，直接影響晶片的頻寬、
功耗與整體運算效能 ，使封裝由過往晶圓製造後的附加製程 ，轉型為半導體關鍵技術 、甚至成為產能瓶
頸，進而帶動技術含量和議價能力提升。
✓ 記憶體與邏輯之間的整合價值是下一階段發展目標 ：為了追求 GPU和HBM能最佳整合 ，台積電透過
2.5D/3D封裝、Die-to-Die互連及Hybrid Bonding等技術，縮短運算與記憶體間的資料傳輸距離 ，可有效
提升頻寬、降低資料搬移功耗 ，並改善整體系統效能 。在進行異質整合時 ，會牽涉到HBM介面、中介層
、散熱設計、邏輯晶圓放置、USB供電標準等，價值鏈從單一製程延伸到系統級整合。

盤勢追蹤

近期焦點
9/7~9/11
美國數據與Fed追蹤：
• 美國8月PPI年增率5.4%，預期5.3%，前值4.8%。
• 財長貝森特宣布，將回購60億美元長天期政府債券，規模相當於一般操作的3倍，然規模未如預期。
• 美國8月CPI月增率從0.1%上升至0.4%，符合預期，為今年6月以來新高；8月核心CPI月增率0.3%，預期0.2%、前值0.2%。其中，無線通訊服務價格月增率達 5.9%，
對核心CPI月增率貢獻約0.1個百分點。
產業/企業動向：
• 媒體報導，美國政府近期與美國煉油商開會討論如何利用國防生產法擴大美國國內煉油產能 。煉油商表示，新建煉油廠需數年才能投入使用 ，傾向提高現有煉油廠
效率。
• 甲骨文盤後公佈FY1Q27 EPS 1.92 美元，預期1.67 美元，整體營收擊敗市場預期。其中雲端基礎設施營收年增率突破100%以上。
• 蘋果公司在秋季新品發表會推出自家首款折疊手機iPhone Duo。新機搭載台積電2奈米製程A20 Pro晶片，展開後螢幕尺寸達7.6吋，售價從1,999美元起跳。媒體報
導，OpenAI目前預計，到2030年算力支出將達到約7500億美元，目前OpenAI仍感覺算力非常不足。
國際市場與地緣政治情勢：
• 媒體報導，波斯灣國家外長計劃 9/14與伊朗外長會面，以討論荷莫茲海峽相關協議 。沙烏地阿拉伯繞過荷莫茲海峽的東西向輸油管遭襲擊後關閉 。媒體報導，美國
部署逾100名美軍顧問至沙烏地境內，支援沙國對抗葉門叛軍。葉門叛軍重申航行封鎖只針對沙國，直到沙國停止侵略、解除封鎖。
• 歐洲央行（ECB）如市場預期升息25bp至2.50%，拉加德稱三種情境下本次升息均經得起檢驗，並上調未來兩年通膨預期，暗示升息週期尚未結束。
台灣：
• 財政部公布8月出口達824億美元，月增9.4%、年增41%，創下歷年單月新高紀錄；台灣出口連續第34個月呈現正成長，追平史上最長紀錄。
• 台積電公布8 月營收，合併營收5,148 億 600 萬元，較 7 月增加 10.1％、年增大幅攀升 53.3％，創下單月歷史新高，並連續四個月改寫紀錄。
9/14~9/18 • FOMC會議、BoJ會議

重點觀察及事件前瞻

通膨風險偏向上行，市場高度定價升息預期
■ 整體CPI符合預期，但核心通膨偏熱。其中，核心服務月增由0.2%加速至0.5%，顯示服務通膨仍具黏性。能源是整體CPI最大推力，能源價格
月增2.1%，其中汽油上漲3.9%，單一項目即貢獻約整體CPI漲幅的三分之一。
■ 核心通膨上升部分來自波動性項目，集中在核心服務項目，如：旅館住宿、機票、教育及通訊價格明顯上漲。其中，通訊費大幅走高，對核心
CPI約貢獻0.1個百分點，若排除該項目，核心CPI可能接近0.2%。核心商品月增則降至0.1%，顯示，關稅尚未造成全面性的商品通膨 。另一
方面，最具黏性的住房與部分醫療通膨並未重新失控，如：房租與屋主等值租金僅月增0.2%，醫療、汽車保險等價格下跌。
■ 債券建議以1～3年期美債及短存續期投資級公司債為主，長天期債券殖利率雖已具吸引力，但在油價未回落前不宜急於大幅拉長存續期間，可
採分批布局。美國期中選舉前市場波動風險仍存，維持輪動格局看法不變，優先布局金融、高股東回報及已展現AI變現能力的科技龍頭與軟體
應用股亦可逢回布局，建議避開高估值、依賴外部融資且財務體質較差的標的。隨著美股接近歷史新高，滿水位者可擇機調節漲多部位；半導
體相關的AI基礎設施則著眼中長線，逢回加碼。

焦點專題：台積電重新定義晶圓代工邊界

✓ 邏輯晶片：重視效能->功耗->面積，用於算力(增強GPU)
✓ DRAM/HBM：重視儲存密度/頻寬->良率->成本，用於餵飽算力(加速GPU記憶體供應系統)
封裝成為晶片設計與製程的延伸
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)
台積電/晶圓代工一線廠 三星、美光、海力士/記憶體廠
定位 先進邏輯晶片代工製造 記憶體製造，三星另有先進邏輯製造
主要產品 CPU、GPU、SoC、AI加速器等 DRAM、NAND、HBM
代表技術 FinFET(過去)、GAA、nanosheet、CoWoS HKMG、MR-MUF、TSV、4D NAND
製程優化方向 高效能、低功耗邏輯晶片，橫向拼合與立體化
(2.5D、3D)先進封裝 記憶體單元微縮化、高層數垂直堆疊
優勢來源 邏輯製程，積累IP、EDA、PDK及長期客戶生態
系
長期專注 DRAM / NAND，累積龐大的記憶體
製程、堆疊和量產經驗
AI時代關鍵 放入更多電晶體的同時降低功耗 提升HBM頻寬/能耗/穩定度

✓ 邏輯晶片與記憶體製程優化方向不同： 雖邏輯晶片與記憶體皆採 CMOS製程，但最佳化方向完全不同 ，
邏輯晶片重視電晶體強度(開關速度/是否漏電/密度/供電/高速互聯)，DRAM強調把位元做小，意即在極小
的平面面積中仍具有足夠電容 (深溝槽/高深寬比/位元線/儲存陣列)，而若走到NAND，則更重視在晶圓上
堆疊上百層存儲單元外，每一層皆可穩定正常運作(高深寬比蝕刻/薄膜沉積/溝道通孔/垂直堆疊/耐用度)
✓ 邏輯製程去做記憶體不具經濟效益： 即使邏輯製程可以做SRAM甚至整合SRAM+I/O+RF，但因需要優化
的部分不同，會浪費很多資金在不必要的方向 ，在成本考量上沒有經濟效益 ，且記憶體客戶希望節省每
個位元的單價 ，而邏輯客戶卻可以為了追求更高效能花更多錢 ，故兩者分開完成後再封裝更具成本優勢
。
邏輯晶片與記憶體製程優化方向不同
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)
邏輯晶片 記憶體
核心目標 高效能、低功耗 高密度、低成本、大容量
製程特色 複雜不規則的電路，有不同尺寸及用途的電晶體 大量重複規則的陣列，由極小的記憶體單元組成
強調重點 電晶體性能、互連效率、元件整合 記憶體單元面積、可靠度、良率

✓ 過去半導體製程中 ，電晶體微縮是首要目標 ，惟走到高速運算系統 ，先進封裝把邏輯晶片和記憶體
(HBM)拉入同一個系統 ，電晶體 、HBM、先進封裝皆會影響整個 AI系統的性能和良率 ，若能將 GPU和
HBM連接更快，則整體效能可進一步提升，故封裝地位顯著提升，成為各家鑽研的項目
✓ 當整個系統從單獨的 GPU和記憶體，變成GPU、HBM、CoWoS、先進互連等全部一起設計時 ，先進封
裝會侵蝕掉一部分原本由記憶體廠掌握的系統價值*，導致HBM價值可能被重新分配。參照台積電技術論
壇提出 、預計2028年開始量產的方案 ，計畫將 14倍光罩尺寸的 CoWoS整合10個大型運算晶粒與 20個
HBM堆疊
*Logic + CoWoS -> Logic + HBM + 3D stacking + advanced packaging
系統性整合時代來臨，記憶體價值部分被重新分配
資料來源：台新投顧整理 (2026/09)

✓ CoWoS為封裝價值提升的典範： CoWoS將多個GPU/ASIC與 HBM高密度整合，直接影響晶片的頻寬、
功耗與整體運算效能 ，使封裝由過往晶圓製造後的附加製程 ，轉型為半導體關鍵技術 、甚至成為產能瓶
頸，進而帶動技術含量和議價能力提升。
✓ 記憶體與邏輯之間的整合價值是下一階段發展目標 ：為了追求 GPU和HBM能最佳整合 ，台積電透過
2.5D/3D封裝、Die-to-Die互連及Hybrid Bonding等技術，縮短運算與記憶體間的資料傳輸距離 ，可有效
提升頻寬、降低資料搬移功耗 ，並改善整體系統效能 。在進行異質整合時 ，會牽涉到HBM介面、中介層
、散熱設計、邏輯晶圓放置、USB供電標準等，價值鏈從單一製程延伸到系統級整合。

貳、公 司 營 運 概 況 
 
一.公司簡介  
上銀為國內精密關鍵零組件製造廠，資本額 35.38 億元，主要產
品包括滾珠螺桿、線性滑軌與工業機器人，上銀生產基地位於台
中之外，於美國、德國與日本等主要機械設備需求地區皆設有子
公司營運 ， 旗下大銀子公司亦與上銀母公司共同購併以色列 -Mega 
Fabs ，使上銀進一步在工業機械人製造產線趨於完成。上銀以自
有品牌「 HIWIN 」行銷全球，上銀已成為全球第三大滾珠螺桿與
線性滑軌廠，僅次於日本 NSK 與 THK。上銀營收地區方面，亞洲
地區 59~64% 、歐洲地區 25~30% 、美洲地區 6~7% 、國內內銷
5~6% 。

二. 2026 年營運概況及展望  
上銀營收主要有滾珠螺桿、線型滑軌、工業機器人與其他四部分。  
 
預估 2026 年滾珠螺桿營收金額 62.00 億元， YoY+26.9%  
 
滾珠螺桿主要功用在於藉由鋼珠於螺桿與螺帽之間進行運動，由
於滾珠螺桿在頻繁返復運轉時，鋼珠間會產生摩擦熱度導致出現
氧化或脫碳現象而縮短使用壽命，上銀技術門檻強調能有效降低
熱源產出，避免熱變形與增加耐久性。滾珠螺桿 2025 年營收金額
48.84 億元， YoY+0.9% 。在台幣升值因素與中國大陸內需疲弱影
響，導致滾珠螺桿營收呈現持平。  
 
滾珠螺桿 1Q~2Q26 營收金額 27.37 億元 ，YoY+19.00%。預 期2026
年，在半導體，精密機械與人型機器人需求增加，將有助滾珠螺
桿需求回溫，預估 2026 年滾珠螺桿營收金額 62.00 億元，
YoY+26.9% 。

2049 上銀(HIWIN)

報告日期： 2026/09/14 研 究 員：洪  國 峰 (Titan Horng)
壹、投 資 建 議

一. 預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 3.30 元
上銀 07~08/2026 營收金額 26.82 億元與 27.08 億元 ，YoY+33.94%
與 42.3% ，MoM+5.00% 與 0.98% 。宏遠預估上銀 3Q26 營收金額
82.10 億元， YoY+36.94% ，QoQ+9.34% ，預估營業利益 12.59
億元， YoY+206.7% ，QoQ+21.79% ，預估稅後盈餘 11.67 億元，
YoY+161.8% ，QoQ+37.71% ，預估稅後 EPS 3.30 元。

二. 預估 4Q26 稅後 EPS 3.46 元
在訂單能年見己見至年底 ， 預估上銀 4Q26 營收金額 84.02 億元，
YoY+29.2% ， QoQ+2.34% ，預估營業利益 13.38 億元，
YoY+324.2% ， QoQ+6.25% ，預估稅後盈餘 12.26 億元，
YoY+165.31% ，QoQ+5.01% ，預估稅後 EPS 3.46 元。

三. 預估 2026 年稅後 EPS 10.80 元
上銀 2026 年在中國製造業景氣復甦，上銀將持續以自身優勢，持
續拓展半導體與精密機械領域 ， 帶動營運成長 。 宏遠預估上銀 2026
年營收金額 305.00 億元， YoY+25.71% ，預估稅後盈餘 38.20 億
元， YoY+150.34% ，預估稅後 EPS 10.80 元。

四. 預估 2027 年稅後 EPS 13.00 元
上銀 2027 年以「驅動實體 AI 時代（POWERING PHYSICAL AI ）」
為核心主題，透過關鍵零組件、致動模組到系統整合方案，在人
工智慧從數位世界走向實體場域，產業競爭關鍵已從 AI 模型延伸
至感測、傳動、控制及系統整合能力，將有助上銀 2027 年營運持
續成長 。 預估上銀 2027 年營收金額 345.00 億元 ，YoY+13.12% ，
預估稅後盈餘 46.0 億元 ，YoY+20.41% ， 預估稅後 EPS 13.00 元。

觀察上銀 2014~2025 年歷史 PER 10~50X ，2026 年 ROE8% ，
PER33.2X ，2027 年 ROE 10%，PER27.9X 。觀 察 上 銀2023~2025
年營收金額落在 240~250 億元間 ，2026~2027 年受惠中國大陸需
求回溫， 營收呈現成長態勢 ，鑑於公司營運己開始恢復成長態勢，
有助評價提升，故投資建議買進，目標價 468 元。 (36X 2027 年
稅後 EPS)

貳、公 司 營 運 概 況

一.公司簡介
上銀為國內精密關鍵零組件製造廠，資本額 35.38 億元，主要產
品包括滾珠螺桿、線性滑軌與工業機器人，上銀生產基地位於台
中之外，於美國、德國與日本等主要機械設備需求地區皆設有子
公司營運 ， 旗下大銀子公司亦與上銀母公司共同購併以色列 -Mega
Fabs ，使上銀進一步在工業機械人製造產線趨於完成。上銀以自
有品牌「 HIWIN 」行銷全球，上銀已成為全球第三大滾珠螺桿與
線性滑軌廠，僅次於日本 NSK 與 THK。上銀營收地區方面，亞洲
地區 59~64% 、歐洲地區 25~30% 、美洲地區 6~7% 、國內內銷
5~6% 。

二. 2026 年營運概況及展望
上銀營收主要有滾珠螺桿、線型滑軌、工業機器人與其他四部分。

預估 2026 年滾珠螺桿營收金額 62.00 億元， YoY+26.9%

滾珠螺桿主要功用在於藉由鋼珠於螺桿與螺帽之間進行運動，由
於滾珠螺桿在頻繁返復運轉時，鋼珠間會產生摩擦熱度導致出現
氧化或脫碳現象而縮短使用壽命，上銀技術門檻強調能有效降低
熱源產出，避免熱變形與增加耐久性。滾珠螺桿 2025 年營收金額
48.84 億元， YoY+0.9% 。在台幣升值因素與中國大陸內需疲弱影
響，導致滾珠螺桿營收呈現持平。

滾珠螺桿 1Q~2Q26 營收金額 27.37 億元 ，YoY+19.00%。預 期2026
年，在半導體，精密機械與人型機器人需求增加，將有助滾珠螺
桿需求回溫，預估 2026 年滾珠螺桿營收金額 62.00 億元，
YoY+26.9% 。

platform ramps from Q4.

items.guidance: AI 伺服器電源 TAM 2025-2030 以 69% CAGR 擴大至 911 億美元(front-end loaded);2027E 強勁:+65% YoY 加速器晶片成長、Rubin 機櫃功率高約 60%、AMD 走向機櫃級系統;400V/800V 於 2028-29 年成為更大驅動;電網可用性與超大規模業者現金流可能於本十年後期壓抑成長
items.trend: AI 電力成為算力的下一個約束條件;功率密度上升使電力電子含量機會大於晶片與機櫃數量所隱含;架構遷移:整合式 PSU → 專用電源機櫃 → 400/800V 配電 → 固態變壓器(SST),擴大每瓦含量,機會橫跨電源供應、儲能、MLCC 與功率半導體;在高壓普及之前,晶片/機櫃/電網層級的架構升級已推動含量成長(2027 年不靠 800V);報告含將加速器預測換算為機櫃、IT GW 與各 GPU/客製 ASIC 平台架構別 BOM 的 bottom-up 模型

SST adoption also represents an expansion and a redistribution of the power-content 
opportunity. In our RF200 scenario, approximately US$706k of upstream SST content is 
partly offset by lower conventional front-end conversion content, producing a net 
system-content increase of approximately US$381k. The supplier opportunity depends 
on capturing good market share on that key transition to more than offset the displaced 
content near the IT rack. 
Turning the BOM into content per watt gives us a common 
denominator
For every platform we calculate power-system content per rack and divide it by the IT 
watts supported by that system. This produces a platform-specific content-per-watt 
metric that allows a 100kW integrated rack, an 800kW power-rack architecture and a 
future megawatt-class system to be compared on the same basis. Blended content/W 
reflects both architecture-specific changes in the required hardware and shifts in 
deployment mix across platforms; it should not be interpreted as like-for-like pricing for 
existing power products. 
At the aggregate industry level, blended content increases from approximately US$0.57/
W in 2025 to US$0.67/W in 2026, US$0.75/W in 2027, US$0.81/W in 2028, US$0.86/W 
in 2029 and US$0.87/W in 2030, maintaining a healthy 9% CAGR from 2025-30. 
Architecture-driven content expansion came first from moves to rack scale systems such 
as Blackwell in 2025-26 and upcoming AMD Helios in 2027 followed by the transition to 
higher-density, externally powered 400/800V systems through 2028-29.   Because 1GW 
of IT load at US$1/W of content equals US$1bn of TAM, the final calculation is 
transparent:  AI power TAM = annual AI IT GW deployed × blended power-system 
content per IT watt.
Strong 2027 growth does not depend on widespread 800V power-rack 
adoption
We see 2026–27 as the principal TAM inflection, as rising accelerator units coincide with 
higher rack density and an architecture-driven increase in content per watt. TAM nearly 
triples in 2026 to US$17.7bn and more than doubles again to US$38.2bn in 2027. 
The 2027 opportunity does not require widespread adoption of native 800V 
architectures. In our model, annual AI IT capacity rises approximately  92%, while 
blended power content per watt increases approximately 12%, together driving 
115% TAM growth. The principal drivers are the scale of accelerator deployments and 
rising system power supplemented by richer power-system content.  We expect a strong 
year driven by the aggressive sourcing plans for accelerator growth including strong 
Google TPU and Amazon Trainium forecasts, still strong power content growth with 
Rubin TDP 60% above Blackwell and AMD moving to a rack scale system with high 
power electronics content. 
The slower initial transition by NVIDIA would shift more of that architecture-driven 
content opportunity into 2028-29 which could at that time offset some of the 
moderation of AI capex. We view Rubin Ultra having only mild upgrade with 30% 
penetration in our base case with modest TDP expansion from 225kW to 250kW but 
likely ramping sharply with the Feynman generation in late 2028 as that has much 
higher chance to move to 4 GPUs per package and 288+ GPUs per rack.  

For custom ASICs, we expect Google and Meta to have about 30% of their 2027 ramps 
of TPUv8 and MTIA v4 with 400V power racks while Amazon would shift similar mix to a 
48V power rack.  With Google designing to EMIB-T and 4 dies on its v9 TPU with 
Mediatek and Amazon a 4 die design for Trainium 4 with Alchip, we model those 
transitioning to power racks in 2028.
While growth moderates, the power track transition keeps the TAM expanding. TAM 
rises to US$55.1bn in 2028, US$75.8bn in 2029 and US$91.1bn in 2030, representing 
annual dollar additions of approximately US$16.9bn, US$20.7bn and US$15.3bn, 
respectively. We view this as a transition from an early units + density + architecture 
growth phase toward a later primarily watts growth phase although still a swing factor 
around architecture upgrades.
Figure 47: AI power TAM growth moderates after 2027, but annual dollar 
increases remain substantial 
Source: UBS
Upside to our out-year estimates would come from higher supported IT power, a richer 
architecture mix, greater storage attachment or higher SST penetration than assumed. 
The extent to which these raise total TAM depends on the additional hardware required 
rather than density alone. 
We would note our TAM covers the power hardware identified in our rack and allocated 
power-rack BOMs including upstream SST content where modeled for Rosa-Feynman. It 
is not an estimate of total data-center electrical capital expenditure which would include 
more of the grey zone equipment.
NVIDIA 800V ramp may start slowly; ASIC power upgrades broaden the 
opportunity
NVIDIA provides perhaps the cleanest illustration of the model mechanics. Within our 
NVL72+ category, physical rack shipments are approximately 27,000 in both 2025 and 
2030—essentially no endpoint unit growth. Yet the average system advances from 
approximately 125kW to 1.2MW if NVIDIA gets to 576 GPUs within a rack by 2030, 
increasing annual deployed IT capacity from 3.4GW to 32.4GW. At the same time, our 
blended content assumption for NVL72 racks rises from approximately US$0.59/W to US
$1.04/W as the architecture adds richer conversion, energy storage, high-voltage 
distribution and rack infrastructure.  The resulting annual power TAM grows from 
approximately US$2.0bn in 2025 to US$33.6bn in 2030, despite essentially flat 
endpoint rack units.  We apply the same framework to HGX, CPU and LPU racks for a 
total NVIDIA power TAM scaling from US$3.7bn in 2025 to US$41.8bn in 2030.

Power TAM growth does not depend on a strong initial 
NVIDIA migration to 800V
The market has focused on the slower migration to 800V and dedicated power racks for 
Rubin, as approximately 440kW of 54V power shelves within the IT rack can support a 
227kW Oberon NVL72 system. Our checks suggest initial power-rack penetration has 
moved lower as the existing architecture can extend through this generation and 
additional time is required to qualify the new high-voltage architecture. The uncertainty 
extends to Rubin Ultra, where a less aggressive upgrade than the original Kyber concept 
could similarly defer the need for external power conversion. A mix of higher GPU power 
and bandwidth but lower memory stack at 8 high nets to only a mild power upgrade to 
250kW. 
Importantly, our sensitivity analysis suggests this is a much smaller risk to the overall 
power TAM than to the 800V narrative. Around our 2027 base case, each 10ppt change 
in NVIDIA power-rack penetration changes total AI power TAM by only approximately 
1%. The larger drivers are the roughly 92% increase in annual AI IT GW deployed and 
higher power content across the broader market, including Rubin’s higher TDP , AMD’s 
move toward rack-scale systems and initial adoption of power racks across custom ASIC 
platforms. Strong 2027 TAM therefore does not require NVIDIA to lead the 800V 
transition.

NVIDIA is also not the only path to externalized power. We expect Google and Meta to 
begin adopting ±400V architectures on a portion of their 2027 deployments, while 
Amazon can continue scaling a lower-voltage architecture with a 48V power rack before 
transitioning to 800V with Trainium 4 in 2028. The timing and topology differ, but the 
common direction is toward higher rack power, greater centralization of conversion and 
richer distribution/protection content.
For 2028, we do see a more mild ramp on Rubin Ultra followed by a strong adoption of 
power racks or initial SST shipments from late 2028 with the Feynman generation likely 
moving to 4+ dies and 288+ GPUs per rack and supporting 800V power side car. We 
model a 30% penetration and around our base case, each 15ppt change in Rubin Ultra 
power-rack penetration changes total power TAM by approximately 1.3–1.4%. We 
model only a moderate initial NVIDIA power-rack ramp, leaving meaningful upside if 
adoption occurs faster, while limiting downside from a slower transition.
By 2028, industry TAM is increasingly diversified beyond NVIDIA architecture decisions. 
We expect stronger power-system upgrades across Google, Amazon and other ASIC 

platforms to support industry TAM even as NVIDIA enters a comparatively modest Rubin 
Ultra upgrade year. This diversification helps sustain our 44% total AI power TAM 
growth to US$55.1bn in 2028 despite slower NVIDIA growth.

GPU and ASIC power remain nearly equally important
Our bottom-up model is also built up for AMD and each major ASIC customer rather 
than applying NVIDIA economics across the industry. Chips per rack, system power, BBU/
CBU architecture, high-voltage topology, dedicated power-rack requirements and 
component content all vary by customer.  We estimate GPU systems from NVIDIA and 
AMD represent approximately 59% of AI power TAM in 2025, 58% in 2026 and 56% in 
2027, before falling to approximately 51% in 2028 and ending at 54% in 2030. ASIC 
systems therefore represent roughly 40–50% of industry power TAM throughout most 
of the forecast.
In dollar terms, GPU power TAM rises from US$3.9bn in 2025 to US$49.2bn in 2030, 
while ASIC power TAM increases from US$2.7bn to US$42.0bn. The architectures differ
—AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI will not necessarily converge on NVIDIA’s 
exact rack implementation—but the fundamental power problem is common: more 
accelerator watts require greater conversion, protection, distribution, storage/
smoothing and downstream voltage conversion while the move up in rack compute 
density through more dies per package and more chips per rack is driving the 
OCP standards move toward power racks and native 800VDC architectures like NVIDIA.
This breadth is important for the investment case. The power TAM is ultimately tied to 
industry AI watts deployed, rather than requiring any single GPU vendor, ASIC program 
or rack standard to dominate the market. We would be explicit that the largest 
uncertainties are not all in the same direction. Accelerator shipment timing can move 
rack deployment between years; accelerators per rack can reduce rack counts even 
while increasing watts per rack; package and system TDP can move the GW 
denominator materially; and BBU/CBU attachment, power-rack sharing ratios, ±400V 
versus single-bus 800V topology and eventual SST penetration can all change content 
per watt.

The 169% and 115% growth rates we currently estimate for 2026 and 2027 could shift 
with product ramps without changing the central conclusion: the AI power market is 
moving from tens of kilowatts per rack toward hundreds of kilowatts and ultimately 
megawatt-class systems, while the architecture simultaneously adds new conversion, 
protection, storage and distribution content.
The critical point is that our US$91bn estimate is not predicated on extrapolating today’s 
rack BOM. It reflects a bottom-up view of how many accelerator systems are deployed, 
how much power those systems consume, where the power electronics sit and what 
hardware is required to deliver each IT watt through successive rack architectures.

AI Power TAM Sensitivities: IT GW is the primary TAM 
driver; architecture determines the upside around it
The two principal sensitivities to our AI Power TAM are annual IT capacity deployed and 
power-system content per supported IT watt. At a constant content per watt, a 10% 
change in our 104.5GW 2030 deployment assumption changes TAM by approximately 
US$9.1bn. Conversely, at our modelled 104.5GW of annual IT deployments, a US$0.05/
W change in blended power-system content changes 2030 TAM by approximately US
$5.2bn.
The sensitivities are not completely independent. Higher rack power can increase IT GW 
while simultaneously changing the required power architecture and therefore content 
per watt; conversely, slower deployment of high-density systems can reduce both the 
GW denominator and penetration of more content-rich power racks. We therefore view 
the sensitivity tables as illustrating the magnitude of individual drivers.
Near-term TAM is most sensitive to IT GW deployed
Our 2027 base case assumes 50.8GW of annual IT capacity and US$0.75 of power-
system content per IT watt, producing approximately US$38.2bn of TAM. Around this 
base case, each incremental 1GW of IT deployments adds roughly US$0.75bn of annual 
TAM, or approximately 2% of the TAM level. A US$0.01/W change in blended content 
adds approximately US$0.5bn, or around 1.3%.
The impact on the year-on-year growth rate is larger because the 2026 TAM base 
remains relatively small. An additional 1GW in 2027 adds approximately 4.2 percentage 
points to TAM growth, while an additional US$0.01/W of content adds approximately 
2.9 percentage points. This reinforces our view that the magnitude and timing of AI 
hardware deployments remain the most important variables for the 2026–27 inflection; 
widespread native 800V adoption is not required for a strong 2027 outcome.

Component price erosion is a risk, but rising system power and 
architectural upgrades mitigate the impact
Competitive pricing is another risk as conventional PSU volumes scale, more suppliers 
qualify and mature specifications such as Blackwell's mainstream 5.5kW PSUs become 
more standardized. However, our bottom-up BOM suggests that single-component 
price erosion has a more modest effect on total system content than changes in IT GW or 
architecture, because power content is increasingly distributed across conversion, 
storage, protection, distribution, controls and downstream DC/DC and also the PSUs are 
upgrading to higher complexity specs moving to 18.3kW and beyond.
Our VR200 integrated-power case contains approximately US$170k of rack power 
content using a PSU-module assumption of roughly US$0.13/W and BBU content of 
roughly US$0.20/W. Reducing PSU pricing by US$0.02/W lowers modelled rack power 
content by approximately 5%, while a US$0.05/W reduction in BBU pricing reduces 
total rack content by approximately 4%.
For the investment case, conventional PSU pricing on mature generations can face 
competitive pressure without invalidating the broader power TAM, particularly as 
additional content pools emerge in high-voltage distribution, protection, energy storage 
and near-silicon conversion. For individual suppliers unable to gain early qualification on 
newer generations of hardware, however, price erosion can still have a larger earnings 
impact depending on product mix and market share.

Storage attachment is a larger architectural swing factor than storage 
pricing alone
BBU and CBU content is less standardized than front-end conversion because 
attachment depends on the resilience architecture selected by the data-center operator. 
A deployment retaining centralized UPS infrastructure may need relatively little rack-
level battery capacity, while hyperscale systems requiring local ride-through or source-
transfer support may attach materially more storage.
For VR200, our base case assumes roughly 50% BBU attachment at US$0.20/W. At that 
assumption, attach-weighted BBU content is approximately US$25.6k per system, 
contributing materially to the roughly US$170k total power BOM. Holding BBU pricing 
constant, moving attachment from 50% to 30% lowers modeled rack content by 
approximately 6%, while increasing attachment to 70% raises content by a similar 
amount. Moving across the much wider 10–100% attachment range produces a 
materially larger swing.
We therefore view BBU penetration as an architectural assumption rather than simply 
another ASP assumption. Greater upstream pooling of storage represents downside to 
rack-level BBU attachment, while increasing requirements for local ride-through, fast 
source transfer and workload stability provide upside. Importantly, lower rack-level BBU 
content does not necessarily imply proportionately lower total data-center storage 
content if capacity is instead centralized into DC UPS or BESS.

SST adoption is the largest out-year architecture sensitivity
The largest architecture-specific swing in our 2030 NVIDIA model is SST penetration. 
Our base case assumes approximately 45% SST penetration, resulting in NVIDIA power 
TAM of approximately US$41.8bn in 2030. Holding the underlying hardware forecast 
constant, eliminating SST adoption reduces modelled NVIDIA TAM to approximately US
$37.2bn, while increasing penetration to 90% raises TAM to approximately US$46.4bn 
under our base SST-content assumption.  
The 45% SST assumption contributes roughly US$4.6bn of incremental NVIDIA power 
TAM versus a no-SST scenario. Each additional 15ppt of SST penetration around our 
base case moves annual TAM by roughly US$1.5bn, although the precise impact varies 
with the assumed power content of an SST-equipped architecture.

SST penetration also has a disproportionate effect on the out-year growth profile. At our 
base content assumption, 2030 NVIDIA TAM growth is approximately 24% with 45% 
SST penetration, versus roughly 10% without SST adoption and approximately 38% at 
90% penetration. 
This highlights why we treat SST separately from our nearer-term 800V thesis: 2026–27 
growth is driven primarily by rapidly rising IT GW and rack power, 2028-29 by power 
rack upgrades and the 2029–30 and beyond growth profile is increasingly sensitive to 
which architecture ultimately wins and how much upstream transformation content 
migrates into the power-electronics opportunity.
SST should also be viewed as a net-content rather than gross-content opportunity. As 
discussed earlier, some upstream SST value displaces conventional front-end rectification 
and transformation. The relevant investment question is therefore not only whether SST 
is adopted, but which suppliers capture the larger engineered system as value migrates 
upstream and which are more impacted by displaced power conversion content closer to 
the rack.

Near-term TAM is driven by GW; architecture matters increasingly in the 
out-years
The sensitivity work reinforces three conclusions: 
1. IT GW deployed remains the largest determinant of total TAM, particularly 
through the 2026–27 ramp.
2. A broader power BOM limits the impact of competitive price erosion in any 
individual component, particularly for vendors able to migrate toward newer, 
higher-content architectures. 
3. Architecture increasingly determines the out-years opportunity: storage 
attachment, external power-rack penetration and particularly SST can materially 
alter both content/watt and the distribution of value across suppliers.
Our US$91bn 2030 estimate does not require every platform to migrate to the most 
content-rich architecture. Rather, the sensitivity work suggests the AI power thesis is 
fundamentally a watts thesis first and an architecture thesis second: rising IT GW 
expands the addressable market, while external power racks, storage and ultimately SST 
determine how much incremental power-electronics content is captured around those 
watts and which suppliers capture it.
Competitive landscape: who captures the 
expanding AI power stack?
Convergence across the white-space and grey-space
The rapid increase in AI rack power is reshaping the competitive landscape across the 
data-center power ecosystem. Historically, white-space suppliers focused on server 
PSUs, rack-level power shelves and board-level conversion, while grey-space vendors 
supplied UPS, switchgear, transformers and facility-level distribution. Higher-voltage DC 
architectures increasingly blur this distinction. Bulk AC/DC conversion, energy storage, 
protection and distribution progressively migrate upstream from the IT rack into 
dedicated power racks, rows and ultimately facility-level systems, while high-ratio DC/

DC and point-of-load conversion move closer to the accelerator.
We therefore see competitive advantage shifting from leadership in an individual power 
component toward breadth across the power stack, qualification with the major AI 
platforms, system-level control capability and the ability to scale from rack-level products 
into multi-MW power systems. Importantly, the opportunity does not accrue uniformly. 
Some suppliers gain incremental content as new layers of power electronics are added, 
while others risk having mature low-voltage conversion content displaced as conversion 
becomes more centralized.
